publicly_readable: The editor's letter (ten trends) in full, via an Internet Archive snapshot. The launch press release. Headlines and one-line standfirsts of the section articles.
not_readable: The body text of the other articles in the issue (roughly 80 to 90 articles, paywalled), the 'Trendlines' data section and the country and industry forecast tables.

entries.quote: Voters will then give their verdict on America’s future in the midterm elections in November. But even if the Democrats take the House, Mr Trump’s rule by bullying, tariffs and executive orders will go on.
entries.subject: US midterm elections
entries.note: Conditional statement. The letter names the event but does not predict the winner.

entries.quote: With luck, the fragile peace in Gaza will hold. But conflicts will grind on in Ukraine, Sudan and Myanmar.
entries.subject: Wars in Ukraine, Sudan and Myanmar continue
entries.note: The Gaza clause is hedged ('with luck'); the Ukraine, Sudan and Myanmar clause is not.

entries.quote: Much will depend on the replacement of Jerome Powell as chair of the Federal Reserve in May; politicising the Fed could trigger a market showdown.
entries.subject: Federal Reserve chair succession
entries.note: Powell's term as chair ended in May 2026; the letter treats his replacement in May as given.

entries.quote: And with rich countries living beyond their means, the risk of a bond-market crisis is growing.
entries.subject: Rich-country bond-market crisis
entries.note: A risk statement, not a prediction that a crisis happens. The launch press release uses it as the headline.

entries.quote: But global emissions have probably peaked, clean tech is booming across the global south and firms will meet or exceed their climate targets—but will keep quiet about it to avoid Mr Trump’s ire.
entries.subject: Global CO2 emissions peak

entries.quote: Better, cheaper GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are coming, and in pill form, too. That will expand access.
entries.subject: Oral GLP-1 weight-loss drugs

notes: The World Ahead 2026 is the 40th edition (press release, 2025-11-10). The editor's letter is mostly themes; only statements about a specific event or outcome in 2026 are captured. Headline-level predictions from the paywalled articles are in the 'headline' entries only where the headline and standfirst were read.
